title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
An online platform generated and hosted non-consensual deepfake pornographic videos using the faces of Dutch celebrities, politicians, athletes, and royal family members. The videos placed victims' faces onto explicit scenes, and the platform incentivized uploads by paying users while enabling anonymity. This is a failure of content moderation at deployment, where a system was operated with no human oversight to prevent illegal material.

The deepfake creation and distribution represents a direct harm deployment of generative AI technology. The victims discovered the content themselves rather than it being caught by the platform's own systems or policies. The failure occurred because the platform prioritized user-generated content and user incentives without implementing detection or removal mechanisms for non-consensual sexual imagery.

It is not established whether the deepfake technology was custom-built, licensed, or third-party software, or what technical or policy safeguards, if any, the platform had attempted before the incident became public. Criminal prosecutions and civil lawsuits were initiated against unknown creators and the platform's operators, but verdicts and outcomes are not reported here.

summary:
Multiple Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in fake pornographic videos on an online platform that attracts 13 million monthly visitors. The manipulated content features the faces of female entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. The interim justice minister has called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file reports. Several victims' representatives have confirmed to NOS that they have either filed complaints or are exploring legal options.

These deepfake videos work by placing a celebrity's head onto pornographic actors in explicit scenes. The platform allegedly pays users who upload material and encourages them to remain anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake pornographic videos will emerge. Deepfake content falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore criminal. Victims have several options including filing reports with prosecutors who may shut down the website, launching collective lawsuits, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma pursued legal action after becoming a victim, resulting in a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
